title: Rise in short-sightedness in children
paragraphs: How's your eyesight? From the moment we're born, our eyes grow, our vision becomes clearer and some of us will have normal or even 20:20 vision. However, others will become short-sighted and end up wearing glasses or contact lenses to help them see everything clearly. And some experts claim that more of us will be wearing them in the future because of our lifestyle when we were younger.

Even today, optometrists are reporting a rise in short-sightedness – also called myopia – in children. The condition can be genetic, but it's also partly being blamed on a number of modern-day factors – particularly children staring at phone screens, computers and game consoles for long periods of time. It's believed myopia also makes them susceptible to secondary eye conditions such as glaucoma, retinal detachment and other visual impairments later in life.

Of course, children have had increased screen time due to lockdowns imposed during the Covid pandemic – it's been the only way to access education and communicate with others. But education generally could be blamed for the rise in myopia. Neema Ghorbani-Mojarrad, lecturer at the University of Bradford, told BBC Future website: "We suspect it is reading and spending more time indoors. Every year of education completed increases the expected amount of short-sightedness."

The problem appears to be more severe in some Asian countries. Some experts say that in these places with huge educational success, children spend more time indoors studying. Therefore, it seems, spending more time outdoors could be good for children's eye health. The UK's College of Optometrists is suggesting parents should get their kids playing outside for two hours a day. Several scientific studies show this can prevent or stop the development of myopia.

There's been a focus on using technology, such as laser surgery, for fixing myopia, but for children at least, it seems a dose of daylight and a break from the screen might be part of the solution. Opticians also recommend kids have regular eye tests to identify any problems before they become more severe.

vocabulary.entry: eyesight /ˈaɪsaɪt/ n. 视力
vocabulary.example: Her eyesight has started to fade as she gets older.
vocabulary.translation: 随着年龄增长，她的视力开始下降。

vocabulary.entry: vision /ˈvɪʒn/ n. 视力；视觉
vocabulary.example: Poor vision can be a barrier to many daily activities.
vocabulary.translation: 视力不佳会成为很多日常活动的障碍。

vocabulary.entry: 20:20 vision /ˌtwenti ˈtwenti ˈvɪʒn/ n. 裸眼正常视力；完美视力
vocabulary.example: She has 20:20 vision and has never needed glasses.
vocabulary.translation: 她视力极好，从来不用戴眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: short-sighted /ˌʃɔːt ˈsaɪtɪd/ adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
vocabulary.example: He's been short-sighted since he was a child and wears glasses every day.
vocabulary.translation: 他从小就近视，每天都要戴眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: contact lens /ˈkɒntækt lens/ n. 隐形眼镜
vocabulary.example: I prefer wearing contact lenses to glasses when I play sports.
vocabulary.translation: 我运动时更喜欢戴隐形眼镜而不是框架眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: expert /ˈekspɜːt/ n. 专家；能手 adj. 专业的；熟练的
vocabulary.example: She's an expert in child psychology.
vocabulary.translation: 她是儿童心理学方面的专家。

vocabulary.entry: optometrist /ɒpˈtɒmətrɪst/ n. 验光师；视光师
vocabulary.example: You should see an optometrist at least once a year to check your eyes.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该每年至少看一次验光师检查视力。

vocabulary.entry: myopia /maɪˈəʊpiə/ n. 近视（医学术语）
vocabulary.example: The study focuses on the causes of juvenile myopia in children.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究聚焦于儿童青少年近视的成因。

vocabulary.entry: genetic /dʒəˈnetɪk/ adj. 基因的；遗传的
vocabulary.example: Some forms of eye disease are genetic and run in families.
vocabulary.translation: 有些眼病是遗传性的，会在家族中遗传。

vocabulary.entry: modern-day /ˌmɒdn ˈdeɪ/ adj. 现代的；当代的
vocabulary.example: Social media is a modern-day phenomenon that has changed how we communicate.
vocabulary.translation: 社交媒体是一种现代现象，改变了我们的沟通方式。

vocabulary.entry: game console /ˈɡeɪm kənˈsəʊl/ n. 游戏机
vocabulary.example: He spent the weekend playing video games on his new game console.
vocabulary.translation: 他整个周末都在新游戏机上玩电子游戏。

vocabulary.entry: susceptible /səˈseptəbl/ adj. 易患（病）的；易受影响的
vocabulary.example: People with weak immune systems are more susceptible to infections.
vocabulary.translation: 免疫系统薄弱的人更容易感染疾病。

vocabulary.entry: secondary /ˈsekəndəri/ adj. 继发性的；次要的
vocabulary.example: The patient developed a secondary infection after the initial illness.
vocabulary.translation: 这位病人在原发疾病后出现了继发性感染。

vocabulary.entry: glaucoma /ɡləʊˈkəʊmə/ n. 青光眼（眼科疾病）
vocabulary.example: Glaucoma can cause permanent vision loss if it's not treated early.
vocabulary.translation: 青光眼如果不及早治疗，可能会导致永久性视力丧失。

vocabulary.entry: retinal /ˈretɪnl/ adj. 视网膜的
vocabulary.example: The doctor diagnosed her with a retinal problem that needed urgent treatment.
vocabulary.translation: 医生诊断她患有视网膜疾病，需要紧急治疗。

vocabulary.entry: detachment /dɪˈtætʃmənt/ n. 脱离；分离
vocabulary.example: Retinal detachment is a serious eye condition that requires immediate surgery.
vocabulary.translation: 视网膜脱离是一种严重的眼科疾病，需要立即做手术。

vocabulary.entry: visual impairment /ˈvɪʒuəl ɪmˈpeəmənt/ n. 视力损伤；视力障碍
vocabulary.example: The charity provides support for people with visual impairment of all levels.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构为不同程度的视力障碍者提供帮助。

vocabulary.entry: lockdown /ˈlɒkdaʊn/ n. 封控；封锁
vocabulary.example: Many people worked from home during the lockdown to stop the spread of the virus.
vocabulary.translation: 封控期间，很多人为了阻止病毒传播选择居家办公。

vocabulary.entry: impose /ɪmˈpəʊz/ v. 实施；强加
vocabulary.example: The government decided to impose new rules to limit public gatherings.
vocabulary.translation: 政府决定实施新规限制公众聚集。

vocabulary.entry: access /ˈækses/ v. 获取；使用 n. 通道；使用权
vocabulary.example: Students can access online learning resources at any time.
vocabulary.translation: 学生可以随时获取在线学习资源。

vocabulary.entry: indoors /ˌɪnˈdɔːz/ adv. 在室内；进入室内 n. 室内
vocabulary.example: We spent the whole day indoors because of the heavy rain.
vocabulary.translation: 因为下大雨，我们一整天都待在室内。

vocabulary.entry: severe /sɪˈvɪə(r)/ adj. 严重的；剧烈的
vocabulary.example: The region suffered a severe drought that lasted for six months.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区遭遇了持续六个月的严重干旱。

vocabulary.entry: laser surgery /ˈleɪzə ˈsɜːdʒəri/ n. 激光手术
vocabulary.example: Many people choose laser surgery to correct their myopia and avoid wearing glasses.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人选择激光手术矫正近视，摆脱戴眼镜的困扰。

vocabulary.entry: fix /fɪks/ v. 矫正；修复；解决
vocabulary.example: This surgery can fix certain eye problems and improve vision.
vocabulary.translation: 这种手术可以矫正某些眼部问题，改善视力。

vocabulary.entry: optician /ɒpˈtɪʃn/ n. 配镜师；眼镜商
vocabulary.example: The optician helped me choose a new pair of glasses that suit my face.
vocabulary.translation: 配镜师帮我选了一副适合我脸型的新眼镜。

sentences.english: From the moment we're born, our eyes grow, our vision becomes clearer and some of us will have normal or even 20:20 vision.
sentences.chinese: 从出生的那一刻起，我们的眼睛就会不断发育，视力会变得越来越清晰，有些人会拥有正常甚至是2.0的视力。

sentences.english: However, others will become short-sighted and end up wearing glasses or contact lenses to help them see everything clearly.
sentences.chinese: 但另一些人则会患上近视，最终需要戴上眼镜或隐形眼镜才能看清事物。

sentences.english: And some experts claim that more of us will be wearing them in the future because of our lifestyle when we were younger.
sentences.chinese: 一些专家称，由于我们年轻时的生活方式，未来会有更多人需要佩戴矫正视力的眼镜。

sentences.english: Even today, optometrists are reporting a rise in short-sightedness – also called myopia – in children.
sentences.chinese: 即便是现在，验光师们也指出儿童患近视眼的比率正在上升。

sentences.english: The condition can be genetic, but it's also partly being blamed on a number of modern-day factors – particularly children staring at phone screens, computers and game consoles for long periods of time.
sentences.chinese: 近视可能与遗传有关，但也有部分原因要归咎于多种现代因素——尤其是儿童长时间盯着手机屏幕、电脑和游戏机。

sentences.english: It's believed myopia also makes them susceptible to secondary eye conditions such as glaucoma, retinal detachment and other visual impairments later in life.
sentences.chinese: 有观点认为，近视还会让他们在日后更容易患上继发性眼部疾病，比如青光眼、视网膜脱落以及其他视力损伤问题。

sentences.english: Of course, children have had increased screen time due to lockdowns imposed during the Covid pandemic – it's been the only way to access education and communicate with others.
sentences.chinese: 当然，新冠疫情期间的封锁措施导致儿童的屏幕使用时间有所增加——这曾是他们接受教育和与他人沟通的唯一途径。

sentences.english: But education generally could be blamed for the rise in myopia.
sentences.chinese: 但总体而言，教育也可能是近视率上升的一个诱因。

sentences.english: Neema Ghorbani-Mojarrad, lecturer at the University of Bradford, told BBC Future website: "We suspect it is reading and spending more time indoors.
sentences.chinese: 布拉德福德大学讲师妮玛·戈尔巴尼-莫加拉德在接受BBC未来频道采访时表示：“我们猜测原因在于阅读以及长时间待在室内。

sentences.english: Every year of education completed increases the expected amount of short-sightedness."
sentences.chinese: 所受教育每增加一年，近视的概率就会相应上升。”

sentences.english: The problem appears to be more severe in some Asian countries.
sentences.chinese: 这个问题在一些亚洲国家似乎更为严重。

sentences.english: Some experts say that in these places with huge educational success, children spend more time indoors studying.
sentences.chinese: 有专家表示，在这些教育成就斐然的地区，儿童会花更多时间在室内学习。

sentences.english: Therefore, it seems, spending more time outdoors could be good for children's eye health.
sentences.chinese: 因此，多待在户外或许有益于儿童的眼部健康。

sentences.english: The UK's College of Optometrists is suggesting parents should get their kids playing outside for two hours a day.
sentences.chinese: 英国验光师学院建议家长每天让孩子在户外玩耍两小时。

sentences.english: Several scientific studies show this can prevent or stop the development of myopia.
sentences.chinese: 多项科学研究表明，这样做能够预防或阻止近视的产生。

sentences.english: There's been a focus on using technology, such as laser surgery, for fixing myopia, but for children at least, it seems a dose of daylight and a break from the screen might be part of the solution.
sentences.chinese: 目前人们很关注用激光手术等技术来矫正近视，但至少对于儿童来说，似乎多接触日光、远离屏幕或许应该是一部分解决方案。

sentences.english: Opticians also recommend kids have regular eye tests to identify any problems before they become more severe.
sentences.chinese: 配镜师还建议，儿童应定期进行视力检查，以便在眼部问题恶化之前及时发现。
